question: does Droid load a Claude plugin root, expand ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, and run its hooks with the literal argument
`claude`
arrangement: a distinctly-named plugin replicating cargento/'s exact layout -- a .claude-plugin manifest directory and a
hooks/hooks.json nested under a top-level "hooks" key whose commands interpolate ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and pass the
literal argument `claude` -- installed at PROJECT scope from a local marketplace, with its own recorder that writes a
file and makes no network call
note: the recorder lives inside the plugin root and the command reaches it only through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, so the hook
firing at all is the proof of expansion. The environment variable of the same name is a separate channel and is NOT
expanded: it still holds the binary's own /PLUGIN_ROOT_NOT_EXPANDED_ERROR sentinel

question: where a mis-routed Droid event lands in the shipped event envelope
note: the id used is a synthetic UUID of the length this probe measured, not one from any session. /api/events/droid is
refused as an unknown harness; /api/events/claude is ACCEPTED and truncates the id to eight characters, while the
collector keys Droid rows on the whole 36. So a mis-addressed event is silently unattributable rather than rejected --
which is the failure that is byte-for-byte identical to a real negative

question: does the shipped Droid collector see a real 0.202.0 session
note: found by running rather than by review, and outside this issue's question: config.py's droid.projects root is
<home>/.factory/projects, and 0.202.0 writes <home>/.factory/sessions/<slugified-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl. With three
real sessions on disk discover() returns False and collect() returns no rows. The per-record parsing is right -- line
1 is session_start carrying id, cwd and title, which is what droid_meta reads -- so only the root is wrong
reading_note: the id_verdict records above carry store_file_named_for_session_id_exists true, and that is resolved against the
OBSERVED root, reached through the payload's own transcript_path. It is not a statement about the configured root,

question: what a Droid Notification payload would carry, and which types exist

call_sites.permission_prompt: the tool executor's batch permission request
call_sites.idle_prompt: the agent stopped by the user and waiting for input

note: this is a read, not a measurement, and it is here because the run that would settle it
is behind the auth gate. It corrects the issue's premise in one place: the four-value
vocabulary the Factory reference documents is three values in this binary, and
auth_success -- the one notifications.py classifies informational and keeps out of
CLEARING_NOTIFICATION_TYPES -- does not appear in it at all

question: how Droid loads a plugin's hooks file, and which event names survive
note: cargento/hooks/hooks.json is searched FIRST, ahead of the Antigravity hooks.json at the
plugin root, so a Droid that finds a cargento root runs Claude's file. Six of its ten
names are in Droid's vocabulary (SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, Stop,
PostToolUse, SubagentStop) and four are not (PermissionRequest, SubagentStart,
TaskCompleted, PostCompact)
silent_drop_evidence: the dropped-with-no-warning half rests on the binary read -- the loader iterates its own
vocabulary and never looks at the rest -- and NOT on a control. No PluginLoader-prefixed
line appears anywhere in the session log, so 'no warning appeared' cannot separate 'the
loader emitted none' from 'this channel carries none'. The missing arm is a condition
known to make the loader log a warning, observed in the same log
